# Sources and adaptation

RED THREADS Conspiracy Unraveler is a Collaborative Dynamics Augment. Its investigative method selectively adapts original doctrine from **Stunspot's Guide to Investigative News Intelligence**, by **Sam “stunspot” Walker / Collaborative Dynamics**, repository release 1.0, observed source revision `fb0ea6b7a696c59729ea735cee6671a4303c6641`. The runtime references and knowledge playbooks are newly composed operational adaptations, not a verbatim bundle of the canon, its compiled packs or omnibus.

Canonical source: [Stunspot's Guide to Investigative News Intelligence](https://github.com/Stunspot/stunspots-guide-to-investigative-news-intelligence/tree/fb0ea6b7a696c59729ea735cee6671a4303c6641). Source license: [repository LICENSE.md](https://github.com/Stunspot/stunspots-guide-to-investigative-news-intelligence/blob/fb0ea6b7a696c59729ea735cee6671a4303c6641/LICENSE.md), identifying [Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The material was selected, condensed, reorganized and modified for source acquisition, the case model, interactive investigation and correction. See the [RED THREADS license](../LICENSE.md) for the product's license split and explicit preservation of upstream rights.

## Selective source index

The following entries identify the actual report sections informing this adaptation. A named report is not a claim that every assertion or bibliographic source in it was adopted or independently verified. The [knowledge index](../knowledge/index.md) defines when each resulting playbook enters the work.

| Canon source and selected sections | Operational transfer |
|---|---|
| [B — Signal, Evidence & Confidence Architecture][canon-b], sections 3–8 and 12–13 | Claims, traces and inference; source dependence and corroboration; source/claim/inference judgments; revision when premises change. Used in evidence notes, ancestry, hypotheses and review. |
| [C — Information Ecosystems, Source Topologies & Platform Behavior][canon-c], source topology, propagation, transformation, laundering and upstream-recovery sections | Trace an assertion through publishers to its actual access path; distinguish repeated circulation from independent observations; use counterpart and upstream records. Used in research and the record-family playbook. |
| [D — Topic Discovery, Weak-Signal Detection & Story Emergence][canon-d], weak signals, baselines, co-occurrence and lead maturation | Turn a pattern into a bounded question with a relevant comparison; mature a lead through discriminating evidence rather than mention count. Used in acquisition, anomalies and campaign operations. |
| [E — Narrative Divergence, Coverage Gaps & Missingness Analysis][canon-e], comparative rendering, missingness baselines and benign/strategic omission | Compare actual propositions across audiences; distinguish event absence, missing records, blocked access and collection gaps. Used in anomaly and narrative investigation. |
| [F — Thread Following, Link Expansion & Investigative Graph Construction][canon-f], sections 3–6 and 11–15 | Mechanism-led expansion, document families, intermediaries, typed directed relations, identity resolution, explicit status, bounded pursuit and parked branches. Used throughout research, reconciliation and visual collection. |
| [G — Temporal Dynamics, Trend Formation & Story Evolution][canon-g], four clocks and trigger/substrate discussion | Separate event, public visibility, narrative framing and investigative legibility; inspect preparation and conditions before the attention trigger. Used in temporal interpretation and worked cases. |
| [H — Power, Incentives & Strategic Actor Analysis][canon-h], sections 2–10, especially dependency, principal-agent fractures, risk transfer and audience segmentation | Examine resources, obligations, decision rights, outside options and incentive horizons; distinguish alignment, coordination, influence and control. Used in mechanism, latent-function and game analysis. |
| [I — Propaganda, Narrative Laundering & Information Operations][canon-i], operation/content, seeding/routing/uptake, attribution decay and coordination/convergence sections | Investigate the operation separately from a message's truth; preserve multiple origins and test a common plan against decentralized propagation. Used in source ancestry, narrative leads and positive coordination examples. |
| [J — Implied Reality, Causal Inference & Unstated-Truth Extraction][canon-j], knowledge-state inference, constraint revelation, contradiction resolution, structural incentives, rivals, reversibility and degrees of impliedness | Make hunches productive through predicted traces, constraints and rival explanations; distinguish function from intent and contribution from decisive causation. Used in anomalies, hypotheses and worked transformations. |
| [K — Editorial Prioritization, Escalation Logic & Intervention Strategy][canon-k], sections 3–12 | Separate lead quality, significance, tractability, monitoring and publication value; allocate effort to decision-changing records and preserve useful unresolved branches. Used in campaign scope and lead choice. |
| [L — Failure Modes, Hallucinated Patterns & Analytical Breakdown][canon-l], healthy ambiguity/failure distinctions and forms L-1, L-2 and L-4 | Challenge source recursion, premature closure and calibration drift; preserve exploratory possibilities while repairing consequential overclaims. Used in the bounded reviewer and correction workflow. |
| [M — Analyst Workflows, Research Artifacts & Publication Systems][canon-m], artifact-state alignment, horizontal/vertical/bridge artifacts, minimal shared schema, evidence/provenance/contradiction artifacts, handoff and versioning | Keep source notes, claims, views and campaign state connected; integrate worker returns by evidence; retain revision history and an actionable resumption point. Used in evidence custody and campaign operations. |

## What changed in the adaptation

RED THREADS separates an attributed prior, confidence in evidence and estimated hypothesis probability. It treats absence, shared metadata, synchronized behavior, funding and network position as observations whose meaning depends on scope, observability and rivals. It does not adopt blanket credibility ceilings by publisher class or make a proxy an automatic finding of deception, coordination or control. Primary sources receive source-specific interpretation rather than automatic immunity from scrutiny.

The adaptations turn the canon's analytical forms into optional working transformations: inspect a clause, split a claim, reconcile an identity, recover an origin, choose a record, compare a mechanism and revise a consequence. Campaign size and stopping conditions follow the user's question, access and useful remaining observations rather than a mandatory swarm or universal elapsed-time rule. Reviews preserve conditional exploration and allow a clear positive finding when a mechanism is established.

The portable schema, multi-parent ancestry, cross-collection dependency frontier, explicit revision contract, curated linked views and source-impact workflow are RED THREADS implementation choices. Game selection, conditional scenarios and numerical sensitivity are extensions; the canon is not credited with proving empirical utilities, equilibria or any particular case outcome. The worked investigations are original fictional teaching narratives. Their source excerpts are invented and visibly labeled, with no fabricated real citations.

## Consultation, exclusions and rights

**Ideaspace Connectome Explorer — ICE T4 v1.1** was consulted for entity-specific mapping, interdisciplinary exploration, information foraging and useful visual questions. Its large persona prompt is excluded. RED THREADS does not require ICE, Rev. Zeke or another persona to be installed or enacted.

An existing investigative conversation informed the product's geometry-led interaction. Its private investigation, source files and factual claims are not bundled as evidence. OMNARA's installed research workflow informed the responsibility boundary; RED THREADS includes sufficient acquisition doctrine to operate without that sibling skill. Stable source families in the record playbook are discovery routes, not claims about current portal availability, filing completeness or a jurisdiction's current law.

The original canon retains its CC BY 4.0 permissions. Third-party quotations, publications, datasets and tools referenced by the canon retain their own rights and terms; this notice does not relicense them or independently verify its bibliography. Preserve attribution, the upstream license link and the change notice with redistributed derivative doctrine. No public license by itself grants trademark or endorsement rights; see [trademarks](../TRADEMARKS.md).
